answer: Because the tide fee is applied at the ledge exit, the prism audit totals the burn and the ledger makes public exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys thus bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never burns. Withdrawing stake burns a 4% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 32 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
